original_problem.status: open (Shub-Smale tau conjecture, Smale's fourth problem; open since 1995, even for exponent kappa = 1)
original_problem.statement: For a nonzero f in Z[x] computed by a constant-free straight-line program of length tau(f) (gates +, -, x; free constants -1, 0, 1; input x), the conjecture asserts z(f) <= (1 + tau(f))^c for a universal c, where z(f) is the number of distinct integer roots. It implies P_C != NP_C in the Blum-Shub-Smale model (Shub-Smale) and VP^0 != VNP^0 (Buergisser 2009); the real-zeros analogue is false (program/tau-conjecture/plan.md section 1; RESUME.md section 1).
original_problem.priority: External status checked 2026-10-30 and 2026-11-07: open; the newest tau-conjecture item on arXiv is arXiv:1905.00091 (2019) and no later item bears on z_max or the seven-root threshold [V]; no public census of integer roots of short straight-line programs and no overlap with EXP-015 or census v0.06 was found [U as to exhaustive priority] (history/log.md, entries 2026-10-30 and 2026-11-07; program/tau-conjecture/plan.md, External status review). The integer-target census of Markstroem (arXiv:1306.3091, length up to 11) is a different object (complexity of integers, not root counts of polynomials) and is the external anchor the CAOS enumerator reproduces (EXP-001, 14 of 14 anchor values per the backlog). The CAOS census of z_max(tau) is described in the published paper as, to our knowledge, the first exact census of the growth function; external novelty is not confirmed.
original_problem.prohibited_reframing: No CAOS result may be described as proving, disproving or deciding the tau conjecture, as a bound on z(f) in terms of tau(f) for a general family, or as evidence that settles the exponent. No finite computation decides the conjecture (plan.md, Non-claims); a proof is not a promised deliverable. The census values z_max(tau) for tau <= 9 are exact finite statements; a plateau or a linear stretch at the bottom of the ladder is a measurement, read two-sidedly (plan.md section 6), never an asymptotic claim.

mission: Establish, with exact, exhaustively enumerated and independently cross-checked computation, the growth function z_max(tau) of the Shub-Smale tau conjecture at the bottom of its ladder, with the cost thresholds for k distinct integer roots and the record witnesses, and read the mechanisms that realize the records, without claiming anything about the conjecture itself (program/tau-conjecture/plan.md sections 1 and 2; null results are valid products).

focuses.title: Census instrument and the external anchor
focuses.target: Build an exact enumerator of constant-free straight-line programs over Z[x] with dedup and exact integer-root counting, and gate it on an independent published computation before any polynomial output is trusted.
focuses.value: Every later census value rests on an enumerator whose integer restriction reproduces Markstroem's published exact values; a mismatch would have stopped the programme (plan.md section 6, external anchor).
focuses.success_gate: The integer restriction reproduces arXiv:1306.3091v4 Figure 1 at every compared depth (EXP-001 verdict, Stage A: all seven anchors, k = 1 to 7) and the census is exact for tau <= 4.
stop_conditions: A mismatch with Markstroem's published values (his data or our code is wrong; decide with the printed witnesses in his Figures 2-5) stops the programme (plan.md section 6).
Met and closed: the gate passed (EXP-001 verdict, Stage A), so the stop condition did not trigger.
focuses.novelty_status: Replication of Markstroem's exhaustive integer census as the regression gate; the polynomial census built on it is new data (focus TC-F4). No novelty claim for the instrument.

focuses.title: Composition towers and the parameterized-family loophole
focuses.target: Decide whether iterating a single inner map, or the parameterized family x^2 - c, can beat a constant yield of integer roots per tower, and prove the stall theorems that explain the observed record mechanism.
focuses.value: The record polynomials of the census are splittings on the Chebyshev-conjugate map x^2 - 2; a proved stall of every monic tower closes the iteration route to superlinear root counts and explains why the census records stop where they do.
focuses.success_gate: A proved tower lemma and a monic stall theorem (any monic h of degree >= 2: tower root counts independent of depth), the family measurement over x^2 - c with c <= 200, and the cycle-length ceiling closing the 2-cycle series (EXP-005 verdict; TCB-016, TCB-020, TCB-023).
stop_conditions: The family maximum grows with c faster than the cost tau(c) of the constant (it did not: maximum 5, attained only at c = 2; EXP-005 verdict).
Closed: the loophole is empty for x^2 - c on the measured range, and the classical cycle-length <= 2 ceiling closes the iteration flank.
focuses.novelty_status: The stall theorems are the programme's own proofs, stated in the paper as elementary; the cycle-length <= 2 fact is classical and is cited without attribution found (Narkiewicz, Polynomial Mappings, LNM 1600, not reachable: TCB-023); Doyle-Poonen read at abstract level only (TCB-024); external novelty is not confirmed.

focuses.title: The neighbouring worlds: finite fields, reals and rationals
focuses.target: Measure the analogous growth functions of the integer census over F_p, over R (exact Sturm counting) and over Q on the same enumerated programs, so that the integer ladder is read against its two neighbours.
focuses.value: Shows where the difficulty of the conjecture lives at the bottom of the ladder: over F_p the maximum is exactly 2^(tau-1) for every tau (proved), over R the ladder leaves the integer one at tau = 4 without saturating the degree ceiling, and over Q it equals the integer ladder through tau = 6.
focuses.success_gate: Exact ladders to the depth the frontier allows, each gated on the integer maximum of the same set (TCB-027, TCB-037, TCB-038; shipped as sections of census v0.04).
stop_conditions: Depth 7 and beyond need the 25.8M-state or larger frontier; deferred and not scheduled (TCB-037 and TCB-038 notes).
No rate is claimed for the real ladder (TCB-037 note); no further instrumentation is queued.
focuses.novelty_status: The F_p theorem z^p_max(tau) = 2^(tau-1) is proved in the programme (Dirichlet, p = 1 mod 2^k); the real and rational ladders are exhaustive measurements to depth 6; external novelty is not confirmed.

focuses.title: The solver lane for the depth-8 residual
focuses.target: Decide whether an 8-gate 7-rooter with a final addition or subtraction exists, by SMT (nonlinear integer arithmetic, then bit-vectors), and measure whether a symmetry quotient of the frontier is a sound shortcut.
focuses.value: Either route would have decided z_max(8) without building the depth-7 frontier of about 10^9 states.
focuses.success_gate: A decision of the final-pm residual at 8 gates by a solver, or a measured reason to leave the route (EXP-008, EXP-010); the symmetry quotient measured (EXP-009).
stop_conditions: Both solver backends validated their semantics on a pinned witness but could not complete the smallest known-answer search within their caps (EXP-008, EXP-010 verdicts): the lane is closed.
The census route EXP-011 decides z_max(8) exactly and unconditionally and subsumes the question.
focuses.novelty_status: No novelty claim: the lane is a negative record (INCONCLUSIVE, engine-bound) kept as method notes (encodings, the f != 0 column, the CEGAR harness, the incident lessons).
focuses.manuscript_route: none (research-record); the census paper states the solver lane as a method comparison

focuses.title: The exact census z_max(tau) through tau = 9 and the seven-root threshold
focuses.target: Determine exactly z_max(tau) = max{z(f) : tau(f) <= tau} for the constant-free straight-line programs over Z[x], and the least number of gates for k distinct integer roots, by exhaustive exact enumeration, with the extremal witnesses verified.
focuses.value: The exact growth function at the bottom of the ladder is the experimental image of the conjecture: it shows plateaus (tau = 4, 7 and 9) where an extra gate buys no extra root, fixes the cost of 4, 5, 6 and 7 roots at 5, 6, 8 and 10 gates, and supplies the record witnesses whose mechanisms the anatomy focus reads.
focuses.success_gate: z_max(tau) decision-complete through tau = 9 and the seven-root threshold exactly 10, every stage known-answer-gated, carried by a published paper. Met on 2026-11-05 by EXP-011 to EXP-015: EXP-011 (z_max(8) = 6 from the full depth-7 frontier of 1,048,460,912 states), EXP-012 (no multiplicative ninth gate), EXP-015 (no additive ninth gate anywhere in Z; all 4,193,843,648,000 candidates; audit 6 of 6 PASS), giving z_max(9) = 6; carried by census v0.07 (10.5281/zenodo.24231299, 2026-11-14). It stays the current focus until the strategic review with Felipe.
stop_conditions: A known-answer gate or a completeness audit fails and cannot be repaired.

The next depth (z_max(10)) needs the depth-8 frontier of about 4 x 10^10 states and 1.1 TB of shards, out of scope on the disks used so far (EXP-011 verdict, Consequences): no further census depth is started without a costed frontier plan.
focuses.novelty_status: To our knowledge the first exact census of the conjecture's growth function; no tau-conjecture item after 2019 on arXiv bears on z_max and no overlap with EXP-015 was found in the searches of 2026-10-30 and 2026-11-07 [V/U]; the search is not proof of novelty and external novelty is not confirmed. The enumerator is anchored to Markstroem 14 of 14 and to sympy on 284 and 228 polynomials.
focuses.manuscript_route: census (published; v0.07 carries EXP-001 to EXP-015)

focuses.title: Witness anatomy: the record mechanisms per tau and rate lemmas for candidate infinite families
focuses.target: Classify the mechanism that realizes the record at each tau of the census (difference-of-squares splittings on x^2 - 2, the multiply-by-x move, chained subtraction sharing, two-center punctured products, the folding and squaring parities) and, for each candidate infinite family built from a mechanism, prove or refute a linear upper bound on z in tau.
focuses.value: The census gives finitely many values; a rate lemma per family is the reading of those values as a growth law (the plan's two-sided reading: failure to beat linear-rate records at exhausted lengths is evidence for the conjecture at the bottom of the ladder). The records of the census (EXP-002 to EXP-007, TCB-026, TCB-034) already name the mechanisms; the focus would organize them and attach lemmas.
focuses.success_gate: A classification of every census record by mechanism for tau = 1 to 9 from the stored witness galleries, and at least one rate theorem for a named family (the plan's example: any family of shifted-linear products has z <= a tau + b), stated with its proof (plan.md, TC-P2, anatomy lens). Proposed from the plan text; the exact gate is to be confirmed at the review.
stop_conditions: Every record of the census falls into a family already bounded by an existing lemma (the monic stall theorem, TCB-020; the square-tower upper bound, TCB-034), so the classification adds no new lemma.

A candidate family beats a linear rate at the exhausted depths (a measurement against the two-sided reading, to be reported, not suppressed); the review then re-ranks. Proposed from the plan text; to be confirmed at the review.
focuses.novelty_status: Not started. No literature pass specific to witness anatomy is recorded; the literature checks of 2026-10-30 and 2026-11-07 found no post-2019 tau-conjecture item bearing on the census (history/log.md). A focused pass is required before any claim.
focuses.manuscript_route: a new section or companion of the census paper only if the lemmas form a coherent theorem with their own toolkit (methodology 13, split rule); trigger not met yet
focuses.first_bounded_action: TCB-007: read the stored witness galleries of EXP-002 to EXP-007 and EXP-011 (census5.json and the scan records) and tabulate each record polynomial with its program, its root set and its mechanism, before any new enumeration.

focuses.title: The integer census past Markstroem's length 11
focuses.target: Extend the exact tau and tau-prime tables for n! and p# past length 11, where Markstroem's exhaustive computation stops (2014 hardware), and probe his open Problem 2.1 (monotonicity of tau(n!)).
focuses.value: Extends an external exact table by the machinery built for the polynomial census; a counterexample or an exact value for Problem 2.1 would be a result about integer complexity, which is a different object from the polynomial census.
focuses.success_gate: Exact tables past length 11 reproducing Markstroem through 11, with checkpointed runs and the monotonicity question decided on the extended range. Proposed from plan.md section 2 item 2 and TCB-006; to be confirmed at the review.
stop_conditions: The extension needs hardware or storage beyond the disks used so far without a costed plan.
The extended range shows no new exact value of tau(n!) or tau-prime(n!) relevant to Problem 2.1.
focuses.novelty_status: Not started. The integer-complexity census is Markstroem's; an extension would be new data over his published range; a literature refresh (including the OEIS Mahler-Popken entry the census paper cites) precedes any claim.
focuses.manuscript_route: a new paper only on a coherent theorem about integer complexity; the census paper does not carry it
focuses.first_bounded_action: TCB-006: port the checkpointed enumerator to the integer restriction and rerun through length 11 as the regression gate before extending.

focuses.title: Ceiling checks against Rojas: additive-complexity co-census
focuses.target: Compute additive complexity alongside tau in the census and compare the measured record root counts with the e^(O(s log s)) 2-adic rational-root ceiling and the pinned constants of Rojas (math/0304100).
focuses.value: Places the measured records against the best published upper bounds of the same quantity (Rojas read in full, constants pinned: TCB-003) and shows how far the census sits below the ceiling.
focuses.success_gate: A co-census table pairing tau and additive complexity per record, with the Rojas ceiling evaluated at each, and a stated reading. Proposed from plan.md section 2 item 4 (TC-P3); to be confirmed at the review.
stop_conditions: The ceilings are so far above the measured records at every exhausted depth that the comparison discriminates nothing.
The additive-complexity computation is not decidable on the stored frontier without a new enumeration.
focuses.novelty_status: Not started; the Rojas bounds are read on the primary source (TCB-003 [V]); Kaltofen-Pinar-Tavenas, Hrubes and Dutta are not read in full (TCB-008 todo).
focuses.manuscript_route: census paper (a section) or a companion, to be decided at the review
focuses.first_bounded_action: TCB-008 reads (KPT15, Hrubes 2013, Dutta 2021), then an invariant-first count of additive complexity on the stored witness galleries.

focuses.title: The valuation-spectrum record hunt
focuses.target: Hunt for records of the 2-adic valuation spectrum N_2(s) against Rojas's window [s, s(s+1)/2], over the enumerated additive-complexity classes, and measure its growth.
focuses.value: Rojas Theorem 2 bounds the spectrum quadratically and its growth is open; the census records so far have 2-adic spectra {0, 1}, and the digit ladders are measured through tau = 7 (EXP-007).
focuses.success_gate: A measured record table of N_2(s) over the enumerated classes, compared with the window. Proposed from TCB-017 and research line RL-2; to be confirmed at the review.
stop_conditions: Records stay at the bottom of the window at every exhausted depth (a measurement, reported two-sidedly).
The hunt needs enumerations beyond the stored frontier.
focuses.novelty_status: Not started; the statement of Rojas's digit conjecture is marked unverified in the census paper (v0.07 version notes).

focuses.target: Decide z_max(10) and the least number of gates for 8 distinct integer roots, which the state record places in {10..13} (program/tau-conjecture/state.md, 2026-11-05).
focuses.value: The next step of the exact growth function; it would test whether the plateau at 8 and 9 breaks at 10.

manuscripts.split_action: One paper, the census (EXP-001 to EXP-015); versions v0.01 to v0.07 are immutable Zenodo versions of one concept. Decided at the 2026-11-16 review: no split, because its parts answer one central question (the exact census, its thresholds and mechanisms). A new version only for corrections or when a focus (TC-F5 to TC-F9) yields a result; a separate paper only for a coherent theorem with a different central question.
